## Current Papers 

### The Limits of Firm-Led Development: Evidence from South African Mining Communities
[Draft](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Su8FBmJKlBsRZP-Xc4hiRn4sGrQ9kLhz/view?usp=share_link) <br><br>
**Type:** Work in Progress (Job Market Paper/Thesis Chapter)  
**Abstract:**  Firm-led development initiatives have become more prominent in recent years, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains limited. This paper evaluates the impact of mining companies’ local economic development programmes (LEDs), which aim to increase incomes and reduce poverty in host communities by promoting alternative livelihood strategies and entrepreneurship. I compile a novel LED project database and combine it with seven waves of geo-coded household data from South Africa’s Gauteng Province. Using an event-study framework, I compare outcomes in LED-receiving areas before and after project implementation. The results show persistent improvements in food security and an increased likelihood of receiving an income. However, effects on entrepreneurship are short-lived, while employment and income remain unchanged. The results are largely driven by alternative livelihood programmes, which promote income diversification. The results suggest that LEDs can reduce markers of absolute deprivation, yet fall short of delivering fundamental change.<br>

### Corporate Social Investment, Political Participation, and Trust in Local Government
Draft available upon request  <br><br>
**Type:** Work in Progress (Thesis Chapter) <br>
**Abstract:**  Through Corporate Social Investment (CSI), companies seek to contribute to the development of their operating areas, taking over responsibilities usually held by local governments. This paper investigates whether CSI affects citizens' government perception and political participation at the local level. I focus on mining-related CSI in South Africa's Gauteng Province and combine information on CSI projects with household survey and electoral data. Using an event study design, I estimate the effects of CSI on political participation, as well as trust in and satisfaction with local government. The results suggest that CSI projects increase community-level political participation, measured by attendance of community meetings, but have no meaningful impact on government trust or satisfaction. CSI-receiving areas show higher participation in subsequent municipal and ward elections, suggesting spillovers to electoral participation. Together, these findings suggest that CSI can mobilise citizens to participate more actively in local politics without weakening trust in government institutions. <br>

### Can Large-Scale Mining Promote Public Good Provision? Evidence from South Africa's Mining Reform 
Draft available upon request  <br><br>
**Type:** Work in Progress (Thesis Chapter) <br>
**Abstract:** This paper examines whether mining can strengthen local service delivery when companies are required to invest in local public goods. I use South Africa as a case study, where post-apartheid reforms introduced such requirements alongside a fundamental overhaul of local governance and service delivery, providing a useful setting for examining their effects. Using census data from 2001 to 2022, I compare access to basic services across mining and non-mining municipalities, focusing on gold and platinum-group metal (PGM) mining and four services: electricity, water, sanitation, and refuse removal. I instrument for mining presence using municipalities’ overlap with exogenously determined mineral deposits and control for baseline levels of service provision. I find that PGM mining is associated with significantly higher access to basic services, while the evidence is weaker for gold mining. These effects are not explained by increases in municipal revenues or improvements in institutional quality. Instead, the results point to a more direct role for mining companies in expanding local service infrastructure, suggesting that corporate investment can help fill gaps in municipal service provision.  <br>

## Other Projects 

### Community Investment Tracker
[CSI Tracker](https://rhinsching.shinyapps.io/project_webpage/) | [Code](https://github.com/rabeahinsching/CSI_Database) <br><br>
**Status:** Ongoing Data Project  <br>
**Abstract:** This is a structured dataset of mining companies’ CSI projects collected from corporate reports using a GPT-based extraction algorithm. Part pf this data is visualised in an online tracker to map investments, identify overlaps, and highlight underserved areas.
